mcqs.learning_point: Relate properties to possible uses of materials
mcqs.question: A material that is transparent, brittle, and a poor conductor of heat is compared with a material that is opaque, flexible, and a good conductor of heat. Which of the following best matches the most suitable use for each material?

options.A: Glass for windows; copper wire for electrical circuits.
options.B: Plastic for water bottles; rubber for building frames.
options.C: Wood for lenses; aluminum foil for insulation.
options.D: Paper for cooking pans; steel for eyeglasses.

mcqs.answer: Glass for windows; copper wire for electrical circuits.
mcqs.explanation: Glass is transparent, brittle and does not conduct heat well, making it ideal for windows. Copper is opaque, flexible when drawn into wire and conducts heat and electricity efficiently, making it suitable for electrical wiring. The other options pair properties with uses that do not match.

mcqs.question: Which statement below is an observation rather than an assumption about a metal rod placed in water?

options.A: The metal rod feels colder than the water.
options.B: The metal rod must be made of iron because it conducts heat quickly.
options.C: The rod will rust over time because it is metal.
options.D: The metal is strong enough to support heavy loads.

mcqs.answer: The metal rod feels colder than the water.
mcqs.explanation: Feeling the temperature difference is a direct sensory observation. Options B, C, and D are assumptions or conclusions drawn without direct observation.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify common physical properties of substances
mcqs.question: Which of the following is a physical property of a substance?
mcqs.explanation: A melting point can be measured without changing the chemical identity of the substance, making it a physical property. Reactivity, combustibility, and toxicity involve chemical changes.

mcqs.learning_point: Compare substances based on observable properties
mcqs.question: Substance X is hard, shiny, and does not dissolve in water, while Substance Y is soft, dull, and dissolves readily in water. Which pair of everyday items best matches Substance X and Substance Y respectively?
mcqs.explanation: A metal nail is hard, shiny and insoluble in water, matching Substance X. Sugar is soft, dull and readily soluble, matching Substance Y. The other pairs do not fit both sets of properties.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand that different substances can have different properties
mcqs.question: Which statement correctly reflects that different substances can have different properties?

options.A: All substances have the same density.
options.B: Substances can differ in hardness, color, and conductivity.
options.C: Every substance reacts the same way with water.
options.D: Physical properties are identical for all materials.

mcqs.answer: Substances can differ in hardness, color, and conductivity.
mcqs.explanation: Option B acknowledges the variability of physical properties among substances. Options A, C, and D incorrectly claim uniformity.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate properties to possible uses of materials
mcqs.question: Which material would be most suitable for a cooking spoon that must not melt at high temperatures and should not react with food?
mcqs.explanation: Stainless steel retains its shape at cooking temperatures and is chemically inert with most foods, making it ideal for a spoon. Plastic may melt, wood can absorb flavors, and glass is brittle.

mcqs.question: A student notes that a piece of chalk leaves a white residue on the blackboard after writing. Which of the following statements is an observation?

options.A: The chalk is made of calcium carbonate.
options.C: The chalk will dissolve in water.
options.D: The chalk is soft because it is used for writing.

mcqs.explanation: Seeing the colour of the residue is a direct observation. Options A, C, and D are assumptions or conclusions that go beyond what is directly seen.

mcqs.learning_point: Identify common physical properties of substances
mcqs.question: A child finds an unknown solid and wants to identify it using only physical properties. Which sequence of observations would be most helpful?

options.A: Taste it, smell it, then see its colour.
options.B: Measure its mass, observe its colour, test if it melts when heated.
options.C: Burn a piece, listen to the sound it makes, then check if it conducts electricity.
options.D: Ask a friend what it might be, then look it up online.

mcqs.answer: Measure its mass, observe its colour, test if it melts when heated.
mcqs.explanation: Mass, colour, and melting behaviour are physical properties that can be observed without altering the substance chemically. Options A and C involve chemical changes or unsafe actions, while D does not involve direct observation.
